Container.Name: cutoffarr
Container.Overview: cutoffarr unmonitors Radarr movies and Sonarr seasons once they have genuinely finished upgrading (quality cutoff AND custom-format cutoff score both reached), so your indexers stop being asked to search for something no release will ever provide. It never deletes, moves, or renames a file, and the only field it ever writes is `monitored` -- never quality profiles, tags, or any other setting. dry_run defaults to true: a fresh deployment writes nothing until you edit config.yml and explicitly turn it off. A small read-only dashboard (WebUI button below) shows each instance's current rest/hunting split, any reverse-scan or file-report findings, and a "Scan now" button to trigger a full sweep on demand -- unauthenticated, since this is a LAN-only tool. See the README (https://github.com/Foley-ops/cutoffarr#readme) for the full config reference, the safety/dry-run guarantees, and how to point each *arr's Settings -> Connect -> Webhook at this container. Mount your config.yml (copied from config.example.yml) at the Config path below; API keys referenced in it as ${VAR} are read from the container's own environment, which you can supply with additional "Variable" entries on this template (Add another Path, Port, Variable...).

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Directory holding config.yml (copied from this repo's config.example.yml). Read-write since v0.2.0 for ONE file: state-cache.json, a copy of the dashboard's own numbers, written at the end of every full sweep and read back at startup so a restart does not blank the page. cutoffarr never writes config.yml and never writes anything else here; the file is display-only and safe to delete. Set this to ro if you would rather not have it -- the write fails with a warning and everything else behaves exactly as before. Your media paths are separate and stay read-only.

Config.Name: Webhook Port
Config.Description: POST /webhook/{instance-name} -- point each *arr's Settings -> Connect -> Webhook at http://cutoffarr:9898/webhook/<instance-name> on the shared network above; publishing this port is only needed to reach the endpoint from outside Docker. Also serves the read-only WebUI dashboard (GET /) and its two JSON endpoints on this same port -- see the WebUI button above.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Timezone (IANA name, e.g. America/New_York) -- used for log timestamps only; cutoffarr's own scheduling is duration-based, not wall-clock.

Config.Name: Radarr Main API Key
Config.Description: Referenced in config.yml as ${RADARR_MAIN_API_KEY} for the radarr-main instance. Find it in Radarr's own Settings -> General -> Security. Rename this Variable's Target if your config.yml's instance name or ${VAR} differs.

Config.Name: Sonarr Main API Key
Config.Description: Referenced in config.yml as ${SONARR_MAIN_API_KEY} for the sonarr-main instance. Find it in Sonarr's own Settings -> General -> Security. Rename this Variable's Target if your config.yml's instance name or ${VAR} differs.
